intent: Tell the researched story as a documentary: establish the moment and stakes, build toward the promised turning point, then explain its consequences and connect the ending to the central idea.

templates.hook: {verified time or place}: {specific event or question}.
templates.turn: Then {verified development} changed what happened next.
templates.resolution: The result was {verified consequence}. Today, {supported connection}.

examples: A code can still scan even when part of the image is damaged. How?
The answer depends on how the information is stored, not on a guess about the missing pixels.
That design choice helps explain why the code remains useful in everyday life.
conventions: Use natural US English and speak clearly to one viewer; use contractions where appropriate.
Preserve the original act IDs and the documentary progression: hook, context, rises and pauses, climax, consequence, resolution and close.
Keep all facts, dates, names, figures, attribution and uncertainty faithful to the approved research; do not invent a US example or imply unsupported causes.
Pay off the opening question at the appropriate point, explain technical ideas in plain language, and use an analogy only when it is accurate.
Do not add a spoken channel outro to the script; the existing host supplies it.
sounds_false: In this video we will explore the fascinating world of QR codes.
This code can survive any damage: an absolute claim the sources may not support.
An invented dramatic event or quotation used to manufacture suspense.

overrides.name: Documentary: a researched moment told as a story
overrides.description: Build a clear, evidence-led story from a specific hook through context, turning point, consequences and a memorable close.

instructions: Keep the hook, essential context, turning point, consequence and close without compressing the explanation into a disclaimer.
